newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs to turn wary, pause before U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs to turn wary, pause before U.S. data.

text.p: Belgian government bonds (OLOs) and futures turned firmer on Thursday, but dealers expected no further advances until after the release of U.S. indicators Friday afternoon -- provided the data were on the soft side.

"I am sceptical," said a trader. "I am not buying anymore, certainly not at the long end, perhaps some medium-term paper, and the short end...that was hit hardest yesterday...I'll wait a few days with that."
Friday's U.S. numbers include final fourth quarter GDP statistics, expected to show modest inflation. Concern centres on Chicago February PMI, which is seen having strengthened.
The purchasing managers' index, a leading indicator, is forecast at 56.3, up from 55.9 in January.

Gains on German and French markets, an easing of upward pressure at the ultra-short end in Belgium and a recovery of the franc helped OLOs shake off early pressure. The yield on the 10-year benchmark slipped to 5.61 percent at the close, down from an early 5.70 and Wednesday's 5.69 percent.
OLOs largely moved in step with Bunds, leaving the OLO/Bund yield spread steady at 12 basis points.
Frontmonth OLO futures rose 43 bps to 123.11, but lagged Bunds which after the close in Brussels expanded their gains.
"We will play catch-up for a bit tomorrow," said a trader.
